source.title: Armagh Guardian, 3 June 1927, p. 3 (list of the new county council: "Returned Unopposed" and "Retiring Councillors deemed to be re-elected"); nominations from the Newry Reporter, 28 April 1927, p. 6 ("County Elections: Nominations in Armagh")
source.publisher: Armagh Guardian (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: every name checked against the two page images; returned unopposed, no poll

note: Triennial election of the county council, 1927: nominations received by Thomas E. Reid, secretary, 26 April 1927; the only poll was in Portadown, 26 May 1927. No party labels are printed for the unopposed members in the nominations or the list of the new council, so none are given. Returned unopposed. John Corkey: no party label printed in 1927. At other elections he stood as Unionist (Glenanne, Armagh Rural District, 29 May 1924, printed 'U': Northern Whig, 1 May 1924, p. 10 ("Armagh Rural District"); Armagh Guardian, 2 May 1924, p. 2 ("Armagh Rural Council": nominations with party labels); Glenanne, Armagh Rural District, 26 May 1927, printed 'U': Armagh Guardian, 29 April 1927, p. 3 ("Armagh Rural Council: General Apathy"); Glenanne, Armagh Rural District, 29 May 1930, printed 'U': Belfast News-Letter, 30 April 1930, p. 15 ("Apathy in Rural Districts") ("Armagh Rural: No Nominations in Fourteen Divisions")). The name stands at elections from 1899 to 1939 and may be a father and son.
